facts.text: Pine Lawn grew around a streetcar line that ran out of the city, with the first subdivisions appearing in the early 1900s.
Natural Bridge Road and Jennings Station Road form the north‑south spine that still defines the town’s layout today.
McDermott’s Edgewood Park subdivisions made up most of Pine Lawn west of Jennings Station, while smaller patches filled the rest of the area.
The historic streetcar stop at Edgewood station was a bustling shopping spot where locals would step off and stroll to nearby stores.
Pine Lawn’s early 20th‑century development was centered around the Pine Lawn station, a key hub on the streetcar line.
The town’s main thoroughfares—Natural Bridge Road, Edgewood, Avondale, Stratford, Kennewah, Jennings Station Road, and Interstate 70—have long connected Pine Lawn to the greater St. Louis area.
